metric: CPU time of the core (src/gcm.c and its envelope) relative to bare OpenSSL EVP AES-256-GCM, which draws a random nonce as the core's random seal does
gate: for each size, the seal and open ratios (GCM over bare EVP) and the det ratio (the deterministic seal over the random one) must be at most the matching ceiling
runner_cpu: to be recorded from the bench workflow
note: A ratio, never nanoseconds, so it is portable across runners. Each benchmark runs five times in a random order and the gate reads the median of the raw repetitions. The ceilings are per size because the core's fixed per-call cost is a larger share of a small message; sizes live in tests/bench/benchmark.cc (kSizes). Refresh recorded_ratios and tighten a ceiling toward the observed worst only when it holds across runs and both libcryptos.
